TcRuntimeType.description: Cm1ChangeHistoryElement is a runtime business object used to present a row of information in a change history table. Cm1ChangeHistoryElement encapsulates the results of navigation of several relations to present the change history of a business object. Cm1ChangeHistoryElement includes details on the authorizing ChangeNoticeRevision object, impacted and solution objects, incorporation details of competing ChangeNoticeRevision objects, and related markup object. Cm1ChangeHistoryElement is used in Teamcenter Change Management Active Workspace area.

TcProperty.description: cm1SolutionItem is a string representation of the solution object's name. cm1SolutionItem identifies the solution ovject related to an element in the context of the business object's change history.

cm1SolutionImpactedItem is a string representation of the impacted object's name. cm1ImpactedItem identifies the impacted object related to an element in the context of the business object's change history.

cm1Markup is a string representation of the markup dataset object's name, which is getting incorporated by the change. cm1Markup identifies the markup dataset object related to an element in the context business object's change history.

cm1AuthorizingChangeNotice is a string representation of the ChangeNoticeRevision object's name. This property identifies the authorizing ChangeNoticeRevision object related to an element in the context business object's change history.

cm1Closure is a string representation of the ChangeNoticeRevision object's CMClosure attribute. cm1Closure identifies the authorizing object's CMClosure attribute state for an element in the context business object's change history.

cm1Maturity is a string representation of the ChangeNoticeRevision object's CMMaturity attribute. cm1Maturity identifies the authorizing ChangeNoticeRevision object's attribute state for an element in the context object's change history.
cm1Disposition is a string representation of the ChangeNoticeRevision object's CMDisposition attribute.

cm1IncorporatesChanges is a string representation of the solution object's name, which is getting incorporated by the object identified by the cm1AuthorizingChangeNotice property of this change history element.
cm1IncorporatedBy is a string representation of the ChangeNoticeRevision objects name, which is incorporating the object identified by the cm1SolutionItem property of this change history element.
cm1IncorporatedStatus is a string representation of the impacted object's cm0IncorporationStatus attribute related to an element in the context business object's change history.
cm1IncorporatedInto is a string representation of the solution object's name, which incorporated the modifications of another ChangeNoticeRevision.

Property cm1SolutionItemObject is a runtime object reference which represents the solution object whose display name is found in associated string property cm1SolutionItem of the same Cm1ChangeHistoryElement object.
Property cm1AuthorizingCNObject is a runtime object reference which represents the authorizing Change Notice revision.

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation gets the merge candidates of a source object that can be merged with the target object in an ACE merge split view where both the objects are part of a change relation. Change tracking functionality in Change Manager tracks changes done on an assembly. ACE uses these objects to render redlining data. This service operation provides a mechanism to view each of these redline changes from source object to target object in ACE split view. Each redline change shows the information of merge operation name, merge component involved and whether a merge is required. Currently the source and target object will act on Assembly BOMs. But in future, they can also act on other revisable objects.
Use Cases:

Use case: Merge candidates in Assembly BOM Merge Split View.
The user creates an assembly and revises it in change context ECN1. The user performs changes like adding a new child or updates BOMLine properties on a revised assembly (target assembly). The user again revises same assembly in another change context ECN2 and perform changes like adding a new child, replacing a child on this revised assembly (source assembly) and releases it. Now, in order to merge the changes from released source assembly to target assembly, the user opens a split view with source assembly and target assembly. The user selects the redline in source assembly and invokes the Merge command, which will trigger service operation to get merge candidates from source object that can be merged into target object. For example, if the user selects a merge candidate Add from panel and click on Merge, then an object of type add will be created in context of target assembly and target change context ECN1.
OperationTemplate.name: Cm1::Soa::CmAws::Changes::getMergeCandidates
OperationTemplate.returnDescription:
A list of objects to be merged, action required and merge status.

The following partial error may be returned:
233075 - The input source and target objects are not valid inputs.
233076 - Change Notice associated to source object is not in a closed state.
233077 - Change Notice associated to target object is not in an open state.

OperationParameter.description:
A source object for which merge candidates need to be retrieved.
The supported objects are WorkspaceObject, ItemRevision or their subtypes.
OperationParameter.name: sourceObject

OperationParameter.description:
A target object with which merge candidates need to be checked if they are merged or not.
The supported objects are WorkspaceObject, ItemRevision or their subtypes.
OperationParameter.name: targetObject

OperationTemplate.description:
This operation sets the active change in the user’s session. An active change applies a context to your current working session that associates revisions with a specific change notice revision object a.k.a. ECN of type GnChangeNoticeRevision. The system offers a list of ECNs as the active changes, those are in open state, not in reviewing maturity where the current user acts as an Analyst or a Contributor.

Once the active change is set, it persists across sessions. The ECN will be set until it is explicitly changed to either another or no active change. The system sets it to no active change when the current change is closed.

When a user makes edits or adds to an impacted item within an ECN, it automatically becomes a solution item with lineage. When a user revises an item the old revision becomes an impacted item and the new revision become a solution item. All solution items appear in the change summary of the Overview tab. If user creates or edits other objects outside of the change context, they are not tracked in the context of the change notice or the change summary.

Setting a change notice as an active change lets you create revisions or property changes that are automatically applied to the active change and are tracked in the change summary. This is very important in a BOM context where a user can add, remove, replace, or modify properties. With an active change context set, these property changes are tracked in the change summary. If active change is not set, these property changes are not tracked.

The default setting is No Active Change. Only a current, open change notice or simple change is available to set as an active change.
OperationTemplate.name: Cm1::Soa::CmAws::Changes::setActiveChange
OperationTemplate.returnDescription: Updated UserSession object in the updated list of the ServiceData. Any failure will be returned in the list of partial errors of the ServiceData.

OperationParameter.description: The object of type GnChangeNoticeRevision that will be set as the active change. If it is null then there should be no active change.
OperationParameter.name: changeNotice

Operation.useCase:
Use case: Merge redlining changes in ACE Split View.
User creates an assembly and revises it in change context ECN1. User performs changes like adding a new child or updates BOMLine properties on a revised assembly (target assembly). User again revises same assembly in another change context ECN2 and perform changes like adding a new child, replacing a child on this revised assembly (source assembly) and releases it. Now, in order to merge changes from released source assembly to target assembly, user opens a split view with source assembly and target assembly. User selects the redline in source assembly and invokes the Merge command, which will trigger service operation to merge changes from source to target objects. For example, if user selects add redline from source assembly and click on Merge, then BOMEdit object of type add will be created in context of target assembly and target change context ECN1.

ParameterInfo.description: MergeRedLineChangesInput object containing information required to merge redlining changes.

Operation.description: This operation reverts changes performed on a BOMLine or standalone object in the Change context. Change tracking functionality in Change Manager track changes done on an assembly in BOMEdit or Solution relation. ACE uses these BOMEdit and Solution objects to render redlining data. This service operation provides a mechanism to revert those changes.
Operation.name: revertChanges
Operation.returnDescription:
The ServiceData contains created, updated, or deleted objects along with partial error if any.

The following partial error may be returned:
    • 43021: The given BOM View Revision cannot be modified. Please check your access rights.
    • 233071: Change can’t be reverted because the ChangeNotice is either closed or not in executing state.
    • 233072: Revert operation can’t be performed. Please provide BOMLine or Selected Object as input for this operation.
Operation.useCase:
Use case 1: Revert redlining changes in ACE.
Users revise an assembly in a change context. After revision user opens the assembly in ACE. The user adds a new line, removes an existing line, updates few BOMLine properties on an existing line, and replaces a line. After performing these edits, changes are rendered as redlining in ACE. Users select one or all the modified lines and invoke the Revert Change command. This command should revert changes back to the original value and clear BOMEdit data automatically. For example, the newly added line after revert action should be removed from the assembly. The deleted line after revert action should be added back to the assembly. The updated property like Quantity, Sequence Number should be reverted to its original value.


Use case 2: Revert redlining changes in object location for revisable object (non-assembly).
When the user adds or removes relations from an object in a Change context, those actions are displayed as redlining data in the object-set table. After these actions when the user selects those redlining data and performs revert changes action which should revert those changes. For example, the added relation should be removed, and the removed relation should be added back.

ParameterInfo.description: A list of RevertRedlineInput containing information required to revert redlining changes.

Operation.description:
This operation sets the active change in the user’s session. An active change applies a context to your current working session that associates revisions with a specific change notice revision object a.k.a. ECN of type GnChangeNoticeRevision. The system offers a list of ECNs as the active changes, those are in open state, not in reviewing maturity where the current user acts as an Analyst or a Contributor.

Once the active change is set, it persists across sessions. The ECN will be set until it is explicitly changed to either another or no active change. The system sets it to no active change when the current change is closed.

When a user makes edits or adds to an impacted item within an ECN, it automatically becomes a solution item with lineage. When a user revises an item the old revision becomes an impacted item and the new revision become a solution item. All solution items appear in the change summary of the Overview tab. If user creates or edits other objects outside of the change context, they are not tracked in the context of the change notice or the change summary.

Setting a change notice as an active change lets you create revisions or property changes that are automatically applied to the active change and are tracked in the change summary. This is very important in a BOM context where a user can add, remove, replace, or modify properties. With an active change context set, these property changes are tracked in the change summary. If active change is not set, these property changes are not tracked.

The default setting is No Active Change. Only a current, open change notice or simple change is available to set as an active change.
Operation.name: setActiveChange
Operation.returnDescription: Updated UserSession object in the updated list of the ServiceData. Any failure will be returned in the list of partial errors of the ServiceData.

ParameterInfo.description: The object of type GnChangeNoticeRevision that will be set as the active change. If it is null then there should be no active change.

TcRuntimeType.description: Cm1AffectedItemsProvider is a data provider that returns CMRelation objects representing affected items associated with a change object. It enables users to view all affected items in a single table. This provider is primarily used in the Affected Items tab of the Change Management application.

Cm1ChangeSummaryElement represents a line row in the Change Summary table in Active Workspace. It is a runtime class that wraps related objects like item revision, usage revision, occurrence, revisable occurrence etc.

TcProperty.description: Property cm1UnderlyingPrimaryObject is an Untyped Reference which represents the underlying primary business object (which typically is the ItemRevision) of a row in the Change Summary table.
Property cm1UnderlyingSecondaryObject is an Untyped Reference which represents the underlying secondary business object of a row in the Change Summary table.

Property cm1SiblingOf is a Typed Reference to the Cm1ChangeSummaryElement to enable grouping of changes of type Replace or Effectivity Split and Cutback. One Cm1ChangeSummaryElement can have many siblings pointing to it.
Property cm1IsLeaf is a Boolean which indicates whether the row has children.
Property cm1Awb0PositionedElement is a Typed Reference to an Awb0PositionedElement which wraps the modified PSOccurrence or Ebm0PartUsageRevision depending on the type of assembly.
